episodes.199293: Severe thunderstorms moved through southwest Missouri during the late evening hours of March 22 and into the early morning hours of March 23. Large hail and damaging winds occurred with these storms.
episodes.199518: Thunderstorms impacted Middle Tennessee during the evening of March 23, 2025. These thunderstorms were generally non-severe, but one particularly thunderstorm intensified in northern Maury County. As it traveled towards the northeast, it had a history of producing large hail until it finally weakened over the northern Cumberland Plateau.
episodes.199600: A cold front moved into a warm, moist airmass and generated thunderstorms. The warm sector airmass had CAPE values of 2000-3000 j/kg and deep layer wind shear around 40 kts with steep mid-level lapse rates all of which was conducive to large hail growth. Storms mostly produced large hail and then also some damaging wind gusts.
episodes.199651: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across far northeastern Oklahoma during the late evening of the 22nd, north of a warm front that was moving through the region. The strongest thunderstorms produced large hail up to ping pong ball size.
episodes.200318: An approaching storm system pushed a cold front southeast through west Kentucky on the evening of the 23rd. Surface-based CAPE around 1000J/kg and deep layer shear of 40-50kts set the stage for a line of thunderstorms to move southeast across west Kentucky through the evening. A few storms within the line pulsed up to produce some small hail, but one stronger storm managed to produce quarter size hail south of Smithland.
episodes.200446: A cold front moved through North and Central Texas on Sunday, May 23rd. As the cold front moved south, scattered storms developed along the boundary and produced large hail. The largest hail fell in Navarro and Henderson Counties, where golf ball sized hail stones were reported.
episodes.200635: An upper level trough and associated surface cold front approached from the west. Convective showers initiated along the front and produced damaging wind gusts across the waters.
episodes.200636: An upper level trough and associated surface cold front approached from the west. Convective showers initiated along the front and produced locally damaging wind gusts across southeast NY.
episodes.200946: After days of high pressure, southerly winds returned and advected sufficient moisture into the area providing ample instability across north Mississippi ahead of a cold front. Typical of March, cold mid-level temperatures provided steep lapse rates. These lapse rates combined with deep bulk layer shear, resulting in large hail and damaging winds during the late afternoon and evening. Storm mode began as discrete cells, before congealing into a line where a quick, spin-up EF-0 tornado occurred in Monroe County.
episodes.200948: After days of high pressure, southerly winds returned and advected sufficient moisture into the area providing ample instability along and south of Interstate 40 ahead of a cold front. Typical of March, cold mid-level temperatures provided steep lapse rates. These lapse rates combined with deep bulk layer shear, resulted in large hail and damaging winds during the late afternoon.
episodes.201217: Relatively strong instability developed ahead of an advancing cold front during the mid to late afternoon hours on March 23rd, owing to strong heating, steep lapse rates aloft and dew points in the 60s. Deeper analysis indicated MLCAPE values of 2000-3000 J/kg, which easily supported robust updrafts. Effective deep-layer shear averaged around 40 knots, with a slightly weaker flow over parts of Texas. However, as thunderstorms developed, they quickly propagated eastward, resulting in clusters of severe storms. As a result, an isolated report of large hail was received during the late afternoon hours near Huttig in Union County on March 23rd.
episodes.201218: Relatively strong instability developed ahead of an advancing cold front during the mid to late afternoon hours on March 23rd, owing to strong heating, steep lapse rates aloft and dew points in the 60s. Deeper analysis indicated MLCAPE values of 2000-3000 J/kg, which easily supported robust updrafts. Effective deep-layer shear averaged around 40 knots, with a slightly weaker flow over parts of Texas. However, as thunderstorms developed, they quickly propagated eastward, resulting in clusters of severe storms. As a result, numerous reports of large hail and a few isolated damaging wind gusts were received throughout the late afternoon and evening hours across North Louisiana on March 23rd.
episodes.202369: A round of severe storms developed during the afternoon of March 23rd and persisted into the evening hours mainly across the northern half of the area. Several supercell storms developed initially, then grew upscale into more storm clusters and ultimately dissipated as a linear system. This main hazard from this event was hail, some large up to 2 inches, then a few instances of wind damage and a lone tornado.
